title: Chocolate and Cigarettes  a collaborative poem—a letter to two forces of two worlds. vast apart.
body:
Chocolate and Cigarettes 
a collaborative poem—a letter to two forces of two worlds. vast apart.


Dear Chocolate,

The trenches birthed, bathed and bred me. Our lives away, my heart still longs to linger. Grounded and rooted in the soil of the slums of the zongo. No space, you haste, you don't live to see the end of the day. Muddy coiled hair, yellow stained teeth, robe that stinks and stinges, making my immediate air gloomy. Lifeless mornings, restless midday, the rest of the day awaits. My light lives away. Away beyond the states beyond the seas. But your hair brings me, no us, near. Your skin and curves, feminine tears, your lust and oh yes! My heart longs to express. No one vies for the crown of elegance when you are near. Epitome of grace; you saved me from buckets of disgrace. Now, I confess that the stick I lit up and the puff of nicotine infused smoke I cough has been nursed into an immaculate and fluffy congregation of angelic clouds.


Dear Cigarettes,

Nicotine deep, clouds deep, no hope in my world only wickedness and torture indeed. I sought for peace but nothing. I found life in a rusted bottle. Guess? It’s love. The sun kisses the rusted rooftops of the zongos even when the cock refuses to crow. I wake up on the bed unwilling to move because I thought sleep was the cousin of death so why won’t I rest my bones? Broken hallelujah, even the pastor refuses to pray for me. My faith on us lingers. Emptied casings, gun hot, makes my body wholly. If I don’t make it home, burn a spliff and burn me. What is love? Stranger to me but I found you, this damsel. A testament indeed. You hold me by the heart and tell me you would allow me breathe. Nothing erotic, just peace. Even after a long day you still make me hopeful that there is light at the end of the tunnel but you don’t know you are my light. Oh my chocolate scented cigarette!



Chocolate: Oh Cigarette!

Cigarette: Oh Chocolate!

Chocolate: When will destiny allow us breathe?

Cigarette: When will our love be allowed in this dark gallows?

Chocolate: Till the rooms clear and peace prevails.

Cigarette: Let's set our differences away in build our third world together. In our minds and hearts. 

Both: Filled with chocolates and cigarettes. A perfect fusion of two worlds.


Writers: Craig Paakow Anderson (Cigarette)
 Privilege Akrofi (Chocolate)
